messages:
alerts-bot: :warning: High token consumption detected on /v1/embeddings (us-east-1) starting 09:12 UTC. Spike concentrated in large-batch requests (>=40 items). System responses include 429s and longer queuing on embeddings workers. Impact: intermittent failures for some paying customers and higher latencies for embedding batches.

juan: I'm on it. Pulling gateway traces and quota metrics. Tara, can you check the quota service logs?

tara: on it. No infra deploys at 09:10. Quota service shows sudden surge of consumption from ~12 api-keys; 3 of those keys are free-tier, rest are paid. Looks like one paid org's CI job is misconfigured and multiplexing many requests concurrently.

ali: Quick mitigation suggestion: enforce a hard max_items_per_request at gateway (e.g., 16) and reduce per-key minute quotas for embeddings route. We can also deprioritize batch traffic by tagging batch UA and routing to background lane.

juan: I like both. Start with hard per-request cap (reject >16 items) and emergency per-key quota for embeddings to 100/min for non-enterprise keys. Keep chat untouched. Anyone object?

ops-bot: Proposed emergency actions (auto-approve if no objections in 60s):
- set gateway rule: embeddings max_items_per_request=16 (400s ttl)
- set per-key override: embeddings limit=100/min for keys tier!=enterprise (30m)
- add header X-Rate-Action=emergency for audits

(60s timer)

tara: Go for it. No objections. Applying now.

juan: Pushing gateway rule: code snippet:
```
# emergency gateway patch
- match: path: /v1/embeddings
  checks:
    - max_items_per_request: 16
    - per_key_limit: 100/min
  exceptions:
    - key_tier: enterprise
  meta: "incident-3001234567 emergency cap"
```

juan: Also added a short-circuit in the worker pool to reject batch requests with explicit error telling clients to reduce batch size (429 with body: "batch_size_exceeded, max 16") so it's clear.

ali: I added a traffic-class rule to tag UA strings like "BatchRunner/*" as BATCH and route them to low-priority queue. That prevents bulk jobs from filling interactive capacity.

(2 min later)

tara: Observability update: 429s on embeddings dropped from 22% -> 6% within 3 minutes. Queue depth on embeddings workers fell to normal. Good signal.

alerts-bot: New metric: rerank route showing slight latency increase (p95 up 120ms) but no elevated 429s. No action needed yet.

juan: Good. Support, please message affected customers and include guidance to reduce batch size to <=16 and stagger requests. @support-bot can you post templated note?

support-bot: Draft: "We've implemented a temporary per-request batch cap and reduced per-key throughput for embeddings to protect overall service. Please reduce batch sizes to 16 or fewer items and stagger requests. If you need help migrating, reply and we'll prioritize."

ali: Two followups we should do before closing: 1) map offending API keys to customers and reach out, 2) add a permanent soft-limit suggesting 16 items and telemetry to detect large-batch patterns.

juan: Agreed. Also flag product: consider adding a client-side SDK validation that warns about batch >16.

tara: Scheduling: emergency rules set to auto-revert in 20 minutes. I will extend if we still see elevated traffic.

juan: I'll handoff in 18 minutes to @ali. Summary for next oncall: emergency per-request cap and per-key throughput applied for embeddings (non-enterprise), batch-tagging and low-priority routing added, support notified, watch embeddings error-rate and rerank latency.

ali: Taking oncall at 09:40 UTC. I'll monitor the dashboards and check infra logs for any secondary effects.

(10 minutes)

tara: Follow-up: located the primary offender - nightly data ingestion job in a partner org set to concurrent=10 and items_per_request=100. Support ticket opened INC-3001234567, vendor contacted. They acknowledged and are patching their job to smaller batches.

juan: Once partner confirms rollback, we can remove the per-key override earlier.

(partner replies via support)

partner: Confirmed. We slowed ingestion to batch_size=10 and added jitter. Monitoring looks good.

support-bot: Partner confirmation recorded in INC-3001234567.

(20 minutes - auto-revert)

tara: Auto-revert triggered at 09:33 UTC. Emergency per-key overrides and max_items_per_request removed. No regression in errors after revert — embeddings error-rate steady at ~1-2%.

alerts-bot: Post-revert check passed. No new alerts in 15m.

juan: Great. Closing incident in monitoring but keeping a follow-up RFC for:
- permanent soft-limits and server-side warnings for large batches
- per-route default quotas split by endpoint (chat vs embeddings vs rerank) documented in runbook
- SDK client validations and examples on batch best practices

ali: I'll own the RFC for batch handling and background lane defaults.

juan: Thanks team. Please add this sequence to the oncall runbook: immediate per-request cap, short per-key throttles, low-priority routing for batch UA, and revert timer. That should reduce time-to-mitigate next time.

support-bot: Notifying customers of incident resolution and attaching INC-3001234567.

juan: Handing off to @ali. Handoff note: watch for any customer escalations, especially around replays where clients may retry with larger batches.

ali: Acknowledged. Monitoring for anomalies now. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:"
